title: How Startups Should Hire Their First Recruiter (November 2026)
summary: Learn when startups need recruiting help, how fractional recruiters compare to agencies and in-house hires, and what to ask first. Updated November 2026.
body_markdown:
Your startup is growing fast, and hiring now takes up hours that used to go toward the product. Most founders are good at vision and execution, not at sifting through hundreds of applications or writing the perfect job post, which makes the[first recruiting hire](https://www.dover.com/) a question of where that time is better spent. A fractional recruiter can take on the sourcing, screening and scheduling workload, so you get back to building the business.


**TLDR:**


-


A first full-time recruiter tends to become worth it at roughly 15-20 hires a year, with fractional help often covering the gap before that


-


The models bill differently: fractional recruiters typically charge by the hour, agencies take a percentage of first-year salary, and in-house recruiters are a fixed salary cost


-


In-house recruiters carry full salary and benefits before tools, instead of fractional options that provide specialized skills on demand


-


Some tools pair a free ATS with vetted fractional recruiters billed hourly, with an average cost per hire of $4,800 across all roles (varies by role and recruiter)


-


Demand for fractional talent across functions, not recruiters alone, has grown substantially as more startups adopt flexible hiring models


## Why Startups Need to Hire a Recruiter


As a founder, you probably started handling all the hiring yourself. You posted jobs, screened resumes and conducted interviews between product meetings and investor calls, but this eventually breaks down.


The threshold for[when to hire a full-time recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/15-20-rule-startup-recruiter) typically arrives around 15-20 hires a year. Recruiting can start to take up a large share of a founder’s week.


**Volume:** You shift from one hire every few months to multiple simultaneous hires, and the administrative load alone becomes overwhelming.


**Quality Standards:** Early hires could learn on the job, but now you need specialists who perform right away, which takes deeper sourcing and evaluation.


**Bad Hire Costs:** A wrong hire at 5 people is manageable, but at 20+ people it disrupts the team and gets costly to fix.


Founder time on recruiting tasks at this stage commonly runs roughly 15-25 hours a week. At a founder’s opportunity cost, that can add up to thousands of dollars a week in lost product and sales work.


## Different Recruiting Models for Startups


When you’re ready for recruiting help, you have four main options. Each has different costs, time commitments and speed of results.


**In-house Recruiting:** Full-time employees who focus solely on your hiring. They learn your culture and keep candidate relationships warm across multiple hiring cycles, unlike project-based recruiters who move on when a search ends. But they require full salary and benefits, roughly $108K a year before tools according to[Workwolf’s in-house recruiter cost analysis](https://workwolf.com/blog/in-house-recruiter-cost/) , plus equity and time to onboard and manage.


**Traditional Recruiting Agencies:** Work on commission, with[contingency placements typically running 15-25%](https://www.pin.com/blog/negotiate-recruiter-fees/) of the hire’s first-year salary, with senior or specialist roles climbing toward 30%. They handle sourcing and screening, but you have limited control over their process.


**RPO Services:** Recruitment Process Outsourcing services take over your entire recruiting operation with dedicated teams and technology for high-volume hiring. They typically require long contracts and large commitments.


**Fractional Recruiters:** Work part-time or project-based, giving you senior recruiting expertise without full-time costs. Understanding[how fractional recruiting works](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiting-employers-guide) helps you see why they integrate with your team while offering flexibility to scale based on your needs.


Agencies seem easiest at first, but[contingency fee incentives](https://www.dover.com/blog/contingency-recruiting-placement-fee-incentives) can work against your timeline and budget. The right choice depends on your specific situation, timeline and budget.


## The Rise of Fractional Recruiting


Some seed and Series A startups appear to use fractional recruiting as a first recruiting resource. The[Fractional Work Report 2026](https://www.fractionaljobs.io/the-fractional-work-report) found fractional talent demand up 149% year over year in Q1 2026, with early-stage venture-backed startups at 36% of tracked postings. The data covers fractional executives across functions, not recruiters alone, from a job marketplace.


Fractional recruiting means staffing your company with recruiters who work a “fraction” of the hours required by a full-time employee. Instead of hiring someone for 40 hours per week, you might engage a fractional recruiter for 10-15 hours weekly or on a project basis.


The economics here make sense. Hourly billing ties cost to the work done, and Dover’s marketplace hires average $4,800 per hire across all roles (costs vary by role and recruiter), and you pay only during the weeks you’re actively hiring.


Fractional recruiters tend to work best inside the same ATS as the hiring team, which gives founders real-time visibility into every candidate and keeps the pipeline with the company once the engagement ends. Some marketplace models pair a free ATS with[vetted fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) in that same system.


## What to Ask a First Recruiter in Late 2026


[Checkr’s 2026 Hiring Hoax survey](https://checkr.com/resources/articles/hiring-hoax-manager-survey-2026) of 3,000 U.S. managers found 40% have interviewed a candidate later revealed to be using a fake identity, up from 31% a year earlier. Before you bring on recruiting help, a short list of questions can save you from costly surprises.


-


**How do you screen for fake or proxy candidates before the first interview?** A strong answer names a specific step, such as a live video screen or a check of ID and LinkedIn history. A weak answer stays vague about process or assumes the ATS catches fraud on its own.


-


**How do you use AI resume review, and where does a human make the call?** A strong answer explains that AI can filter or flag resumes based on criteria the recruiter sets, while a person still decides who advances. A weak answer suggests AI makes the final call alone.


-


**Which ATS will you work in, and does candidate data stay in ours after the engagement?** A strong answer confirms that candidate notes and outreach history stay in your company’s ATS once the engagement ends. A weak answer is noncommittal about data ownership or relies on a system only the recruiter can access.


-


**How are hours and budget tracked week to week?** A strong answer points to hours logged against a weekly or monthly budget you can see in real time. A weak answer offers an informal estimate at the end of the month with no visibility along the way.


-


**What does a typical week of sourcing, outreach and scheduling look like for one role?** A strong answer gives concrete numbers, for example the outreach messages, screens and scheduled interviews they typically target in a week. A weak answer stays abstract about activity without committing to a pace.


-


**Which roles and company stages have you hired for recently?** A strong answer names comparable seed or Series A searches in the same function you’re hiring for. A weak answer stays general about industry experience without naming specific roles or stages.

## FAQs


### How much does fractional recruiting cost compared to other options?


Fractional recruiting is usually billed hourly, so cost tracks the hours you use. Dover’s average cost per hire is $4,800 across all roles, though this varies by role and recruiter. For how that compares with in-house and agency costs, see the Different Recruiting Models section above.


### What if the fractional recruiter isn’t delivering good results?


Hourly billing with no long-term contract means you can reduce hours, pause the engagement or switch recruiters without penalty if results aren’t meeting expectations, and weekly hours tracking shows where the time is going. Dover follows this same model, with performance visible through the hours logged against your budget.


### Can a fractional recruiter work in an ATS I already use?


Yes, a fractional recruiter can work within whatever system you already use, including Ashby, Greenhouse, Lever or a spreadsheet. A free ATS, such as Dover’s, is an option for teams that don’t have one in place. When recruiters and the internal team share the same ATS, candidate data and outreach history stay with the company once the engagement ends.


### Do I need a recruiter if I already use an ATS?


Not always. An ATS organizes the hiring process (job posts, candidate tracking, interview scheduling and reporting), but it doesn’t source candidates, write outreach or run screens. Founders hiring a few roles a year can often manage with an ATS alone. When hiring volume grows or roles get harder to fill, a fractional recruiter can plug into the existing ATS and supply that missing capacity while the hiring team keeps full visibility into the pipeline.


## Final Thoughts on Hiring Your First Startup Recruiter: Fractional, Agency or In-House


The right[first recruiting hire](https://www.dover.com/) depends on how many roles you are filling, how long each search will run and how much of the process you want to keep in-house. Agencies can make sense for a single urgent search, and a full-time recruiter tends to pay off once annual hiring volume is steady. For the bursty, multi-role stretch many seed and Series A teams go through, fractional support often fits the budget and the pace better. Dover is one example of that model: a free ATS paired with vetted fractional recruiters, averaging $4,800 per hire across all roles (varies by role and recruiter) with no long-term contracts. The questions above on fraud screening, AI resume review, data ownership and hours tracking give a practical way to compare options.
